simple.meaning: דֶּבֶק (debeq) is a Hebrew word meaning “a joint ; by implication, solder.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דֶּבֶק (H1694) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 22:34, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דֶּבֶק (H1694) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דֶּבֶק (H1694) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דֶּבֶק (debeq) / H1694 is traced through 1 Kings 22:34, 2 Chronicles 18:33, Isaiah 41:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1694. debeq דֶּ֫בֶק noun masculine Isa 41:7 joining, soldering, appendage — 1 ׳דּ joining, soldering Isa 41:7 . 2 plural הַדְּבָקִים appendages of breastplate (?) 1Kin 22:34 2Chr 18:33 הַדּ ׳בֵּין הַשִּׁרְיָן ובין . (The Be and others compare VB: the jointed attachment or appendage to the rigid breast-armour, which covered the abdomen; > Klo proposes appendage of helmet; Thes suggests armpits, literally joints (compare יָד מַדְבְּקֵי Jer 38:12 ᵑ7 ); Ew the soft muscles etc. connecting the chest with the bottom of the back.)

occurrences.englishText: A certain man drew his bow at random, and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. Therefore he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn your hand, and carry me out of the battle; for I am severely wounded.”

A certain man drew his bow at random, and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. Therefore he said to the driver of the chariot, “Turn your hand, and carry me out of the army; for I am severely wounded.”
So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith.
